summary: Missing free-tier buffer credit for cross-region fallback during hourly billing window
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports they were billed microcharges during an hourly billing window on 2026-03-08 22:00-23:00 UTC despite having a free-tier buffer applied to their org. The charge appears as multiple small invoice line items labeled 'token usage' with no corresponding provisional free-tier buffer offset.

Impact: NimblePulse noticed an unexpected ~$18.40 charge on a provisional invoice for what they expect to be within their free-tier buffer. This affects production traffic that spanned a cross-region fallback event (us-west -> eu-west) during a scheduled canary that coincided with the hourly metering boundary. Customer says this was user-facing (customer-facing chatbot) for ~35 minutes and expects a credit adjustment.

Environment: prod (dedicated capacity), primary region us-west, fallback region eu-west. Model variants in use: redwood-open-7b-q4 (default), gptx-redwood-2.1-quantized (fallback). Keys: api-key ending -np-usw (customer-supplied).

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) 2026-03-08 21:47 UTC: heavy batch of user traffic starts hitting us-west serving pool; KV cache warmup triggered for redwood-open-7b-q4.
2) 2026-03-08 22:10 UTC: serving pool reports resource constraint and routing policy triggers fallback to eu-west running quantized variant.
3) 2026-03-08 22:12-22:47 UTC: traffic is served from eu-west; console displays fallback on request traces.
4) 2026-03-08 23:05 UTC: billing provisional shows token usage lines without free-tier buffer offsets for 22:00-23:00 UTC window.

Expected behavior: free-tier buffer (hourly) should apply across short cross-region fallbacks or be split proportionally; provisional invoice should reflect buffer credit for the affected window.

Actual behavior: meter entries for the fallback window show token counts attributed to eu-west with a tag indicating 'fallback=true' and not tagged for org-level free-tier buffer. Postback reconciler did not attach the hourly-free-buffer tag to those postbacks.

Additional context: Customer provided sample request IDs and timestamps. Links: Slack thread #support-nimblepulse (https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C09SUPP12345/p1678358400000), console trace link (https://console.redwood.ai/traces/trace-ndx-7789), provisional invoice screenshot attached to ticket (not in JSON).
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Desai: Opened ticket after customer escalated to account team. Customer provided provisional invoice and 3 sample trace IDs. Requested immediate provisional credit and engineering investigation into postback tagging.

2026-03-10 Liam O'Connor: Assigned. Noted this looks like a postback-tagging gap during fallback routing. Initial ask: retrieve postback logs for 2026-03-08 21:45-23:15 UTC for NimblePulse org ID and correlate with hourly buffer allocator.

2026-03-11 Customer (NimblePulse - Anika Shah): We need provisional credit today; this is impacting our SRE team budget. Happy to share s3 logs of request IDs and timestamps. Asked whether this is a known issue for dedicated accounts during regional fallback.

2026-03-12 Billing (Marco Ruiz): Preliminary scan shows 18 micro-postbacks from eu-west lacking hourly-tag header. Flagged to postback-reconciler owners. Will prepare provisional credit if engineering confirms missing tag.
investigation_notes: Queried postback-reconciler logs for org=nimbpulse (org id: nimble-357) between 2026-03-08T21:45:00Z and 2026-03-08T23:15:00Z. Found 142 postbacks; 18 from eu-west contained fallback=true but missing header X-hr-buffer-tag.

Routing service logs show a fast path fallback initiated at 2026-03-08T22:10:07Z due to GPU saturations on us-west pool. Fallback completed by 22:12 UTC. Trace samples confirm KV cache warmups on fallback model.

Hypothesis A: Postback instrumentation does not copy hourly-buffer metadata when routing policy rewrites host to eu-west fallback pool. Missing metadata prevents buffer allocator from applying the hourly buffer to those postbacks.
Hypothesis B: Buffer allocator evaluated usage before fallback labeling was reconciled in the postback pipeline due to out-of-order postback arrivals; race condition in hourly aggregator.
Ran reconciliation query joining meter-store entries to hourly-buffer-assignment table. Entries from 22:00-23:00 assigned to us-west were fine; entries reassigned to eu-west lacked buffer pointer.

Relevant logs and queries: billing-query-20260312-hrwindow.sql, postback-log-export://s3/redwood-debug/nimble-357/2026-03-08/, slack thread #infra-routing (link: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0ROUTE99999/p1678430000000).
Related internal tickets: INT-4205 (postback-reconciler: preserve-metadata-on-route-change) — created 2026-03-12 as follow-up.
resolution: Workaround: Billing team issued a provisional credit of $18.40 to NimblePulse on 2026-03-12 pending engineering fix. Engineering next steps: patch postback-reconciler to copy hourly-buffer headers on route rewrite (PR opened: postback-reconciler#514), add unit test for metadata preservation, and add rate-limited alert if X-hr-buffer-tag missing on >5% of postbacks for any org during an hourly window. Owner: INT-4205 assigned to routing team. Follow-up: confirm final reconciled invoice after next billing run and close ticket once customer confirms credit applied in account.
